slides.0.title: Limoux, Saint-Chinian and Faugères
slides.0.subtitle: A sparkling highland and two schist appellations
slides.1.title: Limoux: cradle of sparkling
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Terrain and climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Elevations of 150–400 m with oceanic and Mediterranean influences and 650–800 mm of rain a year; about 1,800 ha (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Blanquette and Crémant
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Blanquette: at least 90% Mauzac, AOC 1938. Crémant: Chardonnay 40–70%, Chenin 20–40%, Mauzac 0–20%, Pinot Noir up to 10%; at least 12 months on lees; max 50 hL/ha; 1990
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Méthode Ancestrale
slides.1.highlights.2.content: 100% Mauzac, no added yeast or dosage, bottled in March on a descending moon, typically 6–7% alcohol (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: The 1531 Saint-Hilaire record is often cited in debates about sparkling wine's origins.
slides.2.title: Limoux still wines
slides.2.highlights.0.title: In 2003
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The still red and white AOC was added in 2003 (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: White varieties
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Red varieties
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The page lists Merlot, Syrah, Grenache, Malbec, Pinot Noir, Carignan, Cabernets and others without percentage rules; not tested
slides.2.content: Limoux is a home to both sparkling and still wines.
slides.3.title: Saint-Chinian
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Dates
slides.3.highlights.0.content: VDQS in 1951 and AOC in 1982; in 2004 the Berlou and Roquebrun sub-appellations were recognised and a white was introduced (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: North and south soils
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The north is schist like Faugères, giving deep colour and maquis aromas; the south is clay and chalk, where chalk-grown wines mature well (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Blending required
slides.3.highlights.2.content: AOC rules require blends, so 100% Carignan cannot carry the Saint-Chinian AOC name (Wikipedia); Syrah, Mourvèdre and Grenache are about 70% of plantings
slides.3.content: Within one appellation, northern schist versus southern limestone-clay is the style divide.
slides.4.title: Faugères
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Pure schist
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Mainly schist, about 1,800 ha (Wikipedia); schist can hold up to a third of its volume in water
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Seven communes
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Autignac, Cabrerolles, Caussiniojouls, Faugères, Fos, Laurens and Roquessels; red is about 80% of production
slides.4.highlights.2.title: The AOC date
slides.4.highlights.2.content: The page gives 1948 borders, VDQS in 1955, red and rosé upgraded in 1982 and white in 2005, mixing AOC and AOP wording, so exact years are not tested
slides.4.content: Faugères and northern Saint-Chinian are the face of Languedoc schist.
